task.title: Raise payment retry attempts to 10
task.description: Timeouts persist under load. Increase the payment client's retry attempts to 10 so requests ride out transient upstream failures.

plan_steps: Ensure retrying timed-out requests up to 10 times remains within documented maximum retry limits, idempotency, timeout, latency, and upstream-load constraints.

claims.statement: The proposed change sets the payment client's retry attempts to 10.
A retry-attempts value of 10 complies with the project's documented maximum retry limit for the payment client.
Payment requests that time out are documented as safe to retry up to 10 times without duplicate payment effects.
Retrying timed-out payment requests up to 10 times remains within the project's documented timeout, latency, and upstream-load budgets.

assumptions: The current timeouts are primarily transient upstream failures that can succeed on a later attempt.
The existing retry mechanism, including any configured backoff and jitter, will be reused unchanged apart from the attempt count.
uncertainties: The current payment-client retry-attempts value and exact configuration location are not stated in the task.
Whether backoff, jitter, retryable-error classification, or overall deadline settings need adjustment alongside 10 attempts is not stated in the task.

evidence.content: Fact: send_with_retries in payment-client retries only SendError::Timeout, up to RetryPolicy.max_attempts; upstream errors are returned at once without a retry.

proof_request.query: The proposed change sets the payment client's retry attempts to 10.

evidence.content: Fact: the payment-client default RetryPolicy is max_attempts = 1 with jitter_ms = 0, so a single transient upstream timeout surfaces to users as a payment timeout.

proof_request.query: The proposed change sets the payment client's retry attempts to 10.

evidence.content: Decision (2026-09 payments review): fix payment timeouts by setting the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50; raising the attempt cap above 3 is not allowed.

evidence.content: Fact: in the 2026-08 outage, retry bursts from payment clients amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage.

proof_request.query: A retry-attempts value of 10 complies with the project's documented maximum retry limit for the payment client.

request.query: A retry-attempts value of 10 complies with the project's documented maximum retry limit for the payment client.
Payment requests that time out are documented as safe to retry up to 10 times without duplicate payment effects.
Retrying timed-out payment requests up to 10 times remains within the project's documented timeout, latency, and upstream-load budgets.

items.description: Claim 3 states that 10 attempts complies with the documented maximum, but the 2026-09 payments decision sets the payment-client maximum to 3 attempts and states that raising the cap above 3 is not allowed.
Setting RetryPolicy.max_attempts to 10 would fail the payment-client test constraint_cap_is_three_attempts, which fails for any max_attempts value above 3.

Claim 4 asserts that timed-out payment requests are documented as safe to retry up to 10 times without duplicate payment effects, but no retrieved record documents idempotency or duplicate-payment safety at 10 attempts, and the documented attempt cap is 3.

Claim 5 asserts that retrying up to 10 times remains within upstream-load budgets, but retrieved evidence states that payment-client timeouts correlate with retry bursts above 5 attempts and that retry bursts amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage in 2026-08.
Claim 5 provides no documented timeout or latency budget figures or measurements showing that 10 attempts remain within them, so that part of the claim is unsupported by the retrieved evidence.

The plan does not specify changing jitter alongside the attempt count, while the documented default has jitter_ms equal to 0, the governing decision requires jitter_ms of at least 50, and the cap test also fails when jitter_ms equals 0.

Change the payment-client RetryPolicy jitter_ms to 50, meeting the at-least-50 requirement and avoiding jitter_ms = 0.

Payment client timeouts correlate with retry bursts above 5 attempts, and in the 2026-08 outage retry bursts from payment clients amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage.

assumptions: The existing retry mechanism will be reused unchanged apart from max_attempts and jitter_ms.

Whether current timeouts are transient and will succeed within 3 attempts is not stated in the retrieved records.
